recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If Financial Management wants PaymentReconciliation.date to become optional in the current build, handle that through a new or separately final cardinality tracker rather than changing FHIR-17997's already-applied add-element decision.
issue_request: FHIR-17997 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Financial Management change request raised for STU3 asking to add PaymentReconciliation.paymentDate as a 0..1 date for the date the payment is issued.
initial_application: The November 2018 financial-resource commit f369c813fb40cd39c0db46336b2b3186f496fb47 lists GF#17997 and added paymentDate to the PaymentReconciliation example and spreadsheet source. Later source rework converted the old spreadsheet to StructureDefinition source, and the published resource surface retained the payment date element.
additional_context: FHIR-26601 later reached Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and explicitly renamed .paymentDate to .date while expanding PaymentReconciliation for patient payments. Current fhir.ini maps PaymentReconciliation.paymentDate to PaymentReconciliation.date, and R4, R4B, and R5 published profiles show continuity of the payment-issued element. A Zulip implementer thread confirmed that paymentDate meant the issued date, not the date funds were received.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. PaymentReconciliation is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/paymentreconciliation/structuredefinition-PaymentReconciliation.xml already defines PaymentReconciliation.date as a date element with short "When payment issued" and definition "The date of payment as indicated on the financial instrument." Restoring the obsolete paymentDate name would contradict FHIR-26601, and changing date optionality from this old tracker alone would be a new current-spec decision.

related_jiras.note: Explicitly renamed PaymentReconciliation.paymentDate to PaymentReconciliation.date and is already represented on the combined branch.
Relaxed PaymentReconciliation.amount cardinality in R6 but did not alter the payment date element, so it does not justify changing date optionality here.
Same 2018 PaymentReconciliation update family fixed status and created cardinalities but did not provide a later decision to change paymentDate/date optionality.
